thread:
ana: Heads up — nightly dedicated CI started hitting OOMs after the batcher/kernel-selection change merged in PR f3a1e9. Seen on both A100 and T4 pools. CI job: `dedicated-nightly-kv-alloc` failed with OOMs and very high fragment counts.

chris: ugh. which commit specifically? any quick repro?

ana: the PR is f3a1e9b (batcher rewrite + kernel pick heuristics). repro locally with `./tools/run_bench --model llm-13b --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kv-cache` reproduces OOM within ~30s for me.

yuki: can you paste the error log?

ana: sure — snip from CI: ```
2026-03-17 03:12:09.842 ERROR runtime.kv_cache: allocate_kv_buffer failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 134217728)
2026-03-17 03:12:09.843 WARN  runtime.kv_cache: fragmentation: total=57.3GB free=4.1GB largest_free=48MB
2026-03-17 03:12:09.843 INFO  serving.batcher: selected kernel=fast_attn_v2 quantized=false seq_bucket=4096
2026-03-17 03:12:09.844 ERROR serving.request: serving aborted, OOM
```

miguel: fragmentation and tiny largest_free suggests small allocation patterns. The batcher rewrite introduced per-request KV suballocations (to reduce tail latency) — maybe combined with fast_attn_v2 kernel we now allocate more small buffers.

chris: I ran a quick profile: before the change p50 token latency was 18ms and p99 120ms; after merge p50 20ms p99 180ms and memory churn up ~+25%. Kernel selection seems to prefer fast_attn_v2 for long sequences now, but its KV memory layout is less friendly to our arena allocator.

yuki: do we have the bisect candidate? can we test reverting only kernel-selection heuristics vs reverting the batching changes?

ana: bisect-ish: `git revert --no-commit d1f9c6a` (batcher rewrite) eliminates OOM locally. `git revert --no-commit 0b7e3c2` (kernel heuristic tweak) reduces fragmentation but doesn't fully fix OOMs. so likely interaction.

miguel: interesting. that suggests the change in allocation frequency (batcher) + different kernel allocation sizes (kernel pick) together push arena to fragmentation cliff. Two mitigation paths: 1) make arena more defragmentation-friendly (coalesce / larger slabs), 2) change batcher to reuse large KV buffers instead of many small ones, 3) fall back to a kernel variant with larger contiguous allocations for long sequences.

chris: for quick mitigation, can we force the CI to pin kernel selection to legacy_attn for seq >= 2048 and keep batcher changes? quick flag at runtime: `SERVING_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_attn` in nightly job. That should confirm kernel interaction.

sre-bot: CI job failed: dedicated-nightly-kv-alloc (build #4521) — OOM during test step `kv_memory_stress`.

ana: I pushed a quick experiment: `ci/force-legacy-kernel` — nightly run queued. If that passes, we can ship a targeted revert for kernel heuristics and keep the batching improvements.

miguel: also adding one-shot diagnostic to dump arena slab histogram in CI when fragmentation > 40% so we get detailed numbers next time. snippet: ```
if (arena.fragmentation_ratio() > 0.4) {
  log.info(arena.dump_slab_histogram());
}
```

yuki: good. also add a stress test variant that simulates mixed sequence lengths (64/512/4096) with KV hot prefixes — reproduces fragmentation quickly. I'll add to `perf/regression` suite.

chris: long term we should add a sequence-length-aware placement policy: prefer kernels that allocate in multiples of our slab size for long sequences. Also consider a small background compaction pass when GPU idle.

ana: update: `ci/force-legacy-kernel` job passed initial smoke but full nightly still running. I'll post results.

miguel: if full nightly is clean, prepare emergency revert for kernel selection change and open follow-up RFC to handle batcher allocation strategy. We shouldn't rollback batching rewrite unless necessary.

chris: agreed. also add a canary gating rule: any merge that changes kernel selection must include KV fragmentation microbench in CI. I'll file an issue.

ana: filing issue now — https://git.internal/r/redwood/issues/4187 — summary + repro + suggested revert.

deploy-bot: Pushed branch `emergency/kernel-pin-legacy` to prevent kernel heuristic rollout to Dedicated prod.

ana: thanks — keeping eyes on nightly. will update when final CI result in ~20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
